basis: April 17, 2023 is the first qualifying disclosure I could verify. J.B. Hunt reported Q1 2023 consolidated GAAP operating revenue of $3,229,588,000 against $3,488,588,000 in Q1 2022, a 7.42% decline and below the $3,314,158,600 cutoff. The earliest public date remains unresolved. The February 8, March 8 and March 14 conference records confirm management appearances, but I could not verify the complete remarks and Q&A or recover the two indexed March slide decks. The numeric upper bound below is the verified actual.

coverage.detail: October 18, 2022 preceding-cycle release reported Q3 2022 revenue of $3.84 billion, up 22%. It gave no Q1 2023 consolidated revenue bound.

The October call transcript search yielded no Q1 2023 consolidated revenue ceiling. The issuer-linked replay at https://players.brightcove.net/5608078629001/default_default/index.html?videoId=6368016247112 returned a cache miss.

November 8 Baird issuer-linked replay returned a cache miss. Baird’s https://www.rwbaird.com/globalassets/pdfs/baird-ic-2022-executive-summary.pdf summarizes the conference and does not establish J.B. Hunt’s complete session.

November 15 Stephens issuer-linked registration page returned a cache miss. The underlying https://wsw.com/webcast/stph33/jbht/1819944 was also inaccessible. The host’s https://www.stephens.com/events/nash-2022-annual-investment-conference confirms the event dates.

January 18, 2023 previous quarterly release reported Q4 2022 revenue of $3.65 billion, up 4%. It gave no Q1 2023 consolidated revenue range. The issuer’s dated posting is https://investor.jbhunt.com/news/2023/01-18-2023-064010885.

January 18 call discussion covered weak demand, possible Q2 improvement and intermodal volume prospects. No numeric ceiling for Q1 consolidated revenue was identified. The issuer-linked https://players.brightcove.net/5608078629001/default_default/index.html?videoId=6368016040112 returned a player page without readable remarks.

January 24 compensation exhibit used annual operating income as a performance measure. The February 9 filing at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/728535/000143774923002843/jbht20230208_8k.htm concerned a director forgoing re-election. Neither supplied a quarterly revenue update.

J.B. Hunt lists all five conference webcasts. Its archived-presentations table exposed template placeholders in the readable page. The event listings identified the following replay targets, but did not supply readable March decks.

Evercore’s two-page schedule identifies the February 8 J.B. Hunt fireside chat, 11:45 a.m.–12:20 p.m., and names John Kuhlow, Darren Field, Brad Hicks and Brad Delco. It contains no remarks. The issuer-linked https://wsw.com/webcast/evercore32/jbht/2349312 returned a cache miss. The indexed transcript at https://www.gurufocus.com/stock/LTS%3A0J71/transcripts/2167766 yielded only an introductory search excerpt.

The February 22 issuer notice names John Roberts and Darren Field for March 8. Raymond James’s https://www.raymondjames.com/-/media/rj/dotcom/files/corporations-and-institutions/equity-capital-markets/corporate-access-events.pdf is an event calendar. The issuer-linked session https://wsw.com/webcast/rj127/jbht/1594544 returned a cache miss.

The March 1 issuer notice names Shelley Simpson and Darren Field for March 14. The host session https://jpmorgan.metameetings.net/events/industrials23/sessions/45011-j-b-hunt-transport-services-inc/webcast?gpu_only=true&kiosk=true returned a cache miss. The same URL without its query was inaccessible. The preview at https://www.gurufocus.com/stock/JBHT/transcripts/2167768 confirms slides followed by planned Q&A, then cuts off during Simpson’s opening remarks.

The index identifies separate March 8 and March 14 decks. Both document targets returned cache misses: https://stockanalysis.com/filings/JBHT/1503525/ and https://stockanalysis.com/filings/JBHT/1503592/. The three transcript targets also returned cache misses: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/jbht/transcripts/423382-evercore-isi-travel-transport-conference/, https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/jbht/transcripts/57926-raymond-james-institutional-investors-conference/ and https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/jbht/transcripts/58745-jpmorgan-industrials-conference/.

Snapshot availability could not be verified. This lookup and the corresponding https://archive.org/wayback/available?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwsw.com%2Fwebcast%2Frj127%2Fjbht%2F1594544 and https://archive.org/wayback/available?url=https%3A%2F%2Fjpmorgan.metameetings.net%2Fevents%2Findustrials23%2Fsessions%2F45011-j-b-hunt-transport-services-inc%2Fwebcast were inaccessible.
April 3 issuer notice scheduled Q1 results for market close April 17. It gave no preliminary revenue figure.

April 17 Exhibit 99.1 gives total operating revenue including fuel surcharges of 3,229,588 and 3,488,588 in thousands for the three months ended March 31, 2023 and 2022. The segment table independently reconciles both totals after intersegment eliminations. January transfers were internal. The reported comparison includes Zenith’s acquisition contribution.

publication_date_evidence: Exhibit 99.1 is marked “FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE” and dated April 17, 2023. J.B. Hunt’s newsroom independently displays April 17, 2023 and reports the Q1 revenue decline at https://www.jbhunt.com/our-company/newsroom/2023/04/q1-2023-earnings. This verifies the actual-results publication date. Incomplete conference records prevent assigning it as the earliest date.
